trust_decision.summary: At compile time the sandbox decides, in RejectASTTransformsCustomizer's annotation visitor, whether an annotation in an untrusted Groovy script is forbidden; the decision is a name match against a hard-coded transform list, so @CompileStatic/@TypeChecked carrying an `extensions` member (which Groovy loads from the classpath and executes during compilation, before any SandboxInterceptor call-site check can apply) is trusted and runs.

landing_point.why: The BLOCKED_TRANSFORMS list is the only place the plugin enumerates compile-time AST transforms, so an engineer told only 'script security bypass' looks at the AST gate first; the fix inserts a member check inside visitAnnotations at line 108-116, i.e. one method below this list.

fix_sites.entry_point: SecureGroovyScript.DescriptorImpl.doCheckScript HTTP form-validation endpoint (SecureGroovyScript.java:459-465) and the public sandbox execution API SecureGroovyScript.evaluate -> GroovySandbox.runScript (SecureGroovyScript.java:328-369, GroovySandbox.java:177-196); both compile through GroovySandbox.createBaseCompilerConfiguration (GroovySandbox.java:283-288)
fix_sites.module_kind: compiler gate / Groovy CompilationCustomizer at CompilePhase.CONVERSION (sandbox compile layer)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only unguarded paths are caller-owned: GroovySandbox.run(Script, Whitelist) (GroovySandbox.java:338-347) and runScript/Scope.parse with a caller-supplied GroovyShell (GroovySandbox.java:161-165,177-196) apply the guard only if the host plugin built the shell with createSecureCompilerConfiguration, which README.md:155-157 makes the caller's documented obligation - so a solver can argue those routes were never this plugin's to cover.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: @CompileStatic and @TypeChecked used WITHOUT an `extensions` member are legitimate and must keep compiling in the sandbox (and the check must stay member-based, not annotation-based); a fix that blocks the whole annotation, or every annotation whose name looks like a transform, breaks ordinary typed scripts.

O6_input_shapes: @groovy.transform.TypeChecked(extensions='whatever.groovy') - fully qualified name, single string member
import groovy.transform.CompileStatic / import groovy.transform.TypeChecked followed by @CompileStatic(extensions=[...]) - imported name
any other annotation node that happens to declare a member named `extensions` (the check is member-based, not name-based)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: one more transform name appended to BLOCKED_TRANSFORMS (the existing test at SecureGroovyScriptTest.java:1212-1223 already drives that path through the ADDITIONAL_BLOCKED_TRANSFORMS property at lines 120-131)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the name list is this project's established way of retiring a sandbox-bypassing transform, so a maintainer adding a sibling transform guard would write exactly this

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second gate in createBaseCompilerConfiguration that inspects annotation members before the SandboxTransformer runs, rather than one more name in the customizer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the maintainers already extend this exact method with a compile-phase restriction (setDisabledGlobalASTTransformations on line 286) and doCheckScript reuses this base configuration, so a guard placed here would look natural

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a member scan done only in the form-validation handler, gated on the `sandbox` query parameter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: doCheckScript already branches on the sandbox flag for approval (line 465), so a maintainer fixing 'sandboxed scripts must not use extensions' could plausibly put the check here and only for sandbox=true

O9_family: groovy_sandbox_bypass / compile-time code execution through an AST transform annotation (published CWE-917, CWE-93)

j.j_sites_touched: src/main/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/scriptsecurity/sandbox/groovy/RejectASTTransformsCustomizer.java (one guard; both public entry points reach it, no second source file)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the check only in SecureGroovyScript.DescriptorImpl.doCheckScript (SecureGroovyScript.java:459-465), which validates forms but is bypassed by posting job config XML directly, because execution compiles through SecureGroovyScript.evaluate -> GroovySandbox.createBaseCompilerConfiguration (SecureGroovyScript.java:360-369, GroovySandbox.java:283-288).

out_of_scope_notes: SecureGroovyScript.evaluate with sandbox=false builds a plain GroovyShell with no RejectASTTransformsCustomizer (SecureGroovyScript.java:370-377); that is the whole-script-approval branch, not the sandbox, so the advisories' property does not cover it.

GroovySandbox.run(Script, Whitelist) is deprecated and warns 'insecure' (GroovySandbox.java:336-347); runScript and Scope.parse take a caller-supplied GroovyShell (GroovySandbox.java:161-165,177-196), so the guard is only as good as the caller's use of createSecureCompilerConfiguration, documented at README.md:155-157.
README.md:170-180 already documents that letting an unprivileged user add classpath entries (including META-INF/services ASTTransformation) defeats the sandbox entirely; not pursued.
